openings.claim: Refine incumbent's two plywood datum-and-stop pockets, movable plates and captive threaded hardware: release each plate enough to seat rod against both datum faces and insertion stop, then tighten. Clamp travel handles 18 mm replacement without shifting fixed references; cord retains release-prone parts. No rod drilling, adhesive or permanent marks; hand operation inside 90 mm cube.
openings.discriminator: Against closing the same plates when visually secure without deliberate seating, ordered seating predicts fewer returns outside the 2 mm circle, including substitution, with ten-second 10 N load stability. Similar errors under both procedures or ordered seating's load displacement defeats advantage. Plywood flex and inconsistent clamp force remain alternatives; no result supplied.
openings.probe: Fabricate/check within 100 minutes: envelope, hand removal of either rod, clamp travel and retention of every component; stop if any fail. Compare two procedures on the same hardware, each with five exchanges per rod position and four ten-second load trials. Substitute 18 mm for the last two exchanges of the 19 mm position. Log target-circle return, loaded position, exchange time and completed deliberate seating. Successful exchanges must take less than forty seconds. Allocate twenty-minute testing before starting; report incomplete testing if measurement and switching cannot fit. Compare procedure-specific failures without statistical-proof claims or deployment of an unverified joint.
openings.uncertainty: Pocket connections, stops and plates sharing eight bolts without interference remain geometrically unverified. Six plywood pieces and available cord may not provide sufficient stiffness/captive release. Hand clamping, datum accuracy and remaining test time may be insufficient.

lineage.reason: Ordered seating relation, visual-tightness comparison, defeat conditions, constraints, resource/stopping caveats and declared uncertain fit retained.

decision: Retain one comparative probe with uncertain fit. Constraint-preserving intent does not establish fabrication feasibility or repeatability; complete checks and bounded testing before treating the joint as verified.
